# Hybrid and Remote Work Policy

## Purpose and scope

Lumen Ridge Software, Inc. supports flexible work while maintaining collaboration, customer service, security, and legal compliance. This policy applies to all employees and replaces Memos A, B, and C and any conflicting hybrid or remote-work guidance.

Employees must follow their approved work arrangement. Remote work does not change performance expectations, availability requirements, or employment terms.

## Work arrangements (onsite / hybrid / remote, and who falls into which)

People will confirm each employee’s arrangement in writing:

- **Onsite:** Roles requiring regular physical presence, as designated by the manager and People. Employees work at their assigned office on scheduled workdays.
- **Hybrid:** Employees whose approved home worksite is within a 50-mile straight-line radius of a company office, unless designated onsite or granted an exception.
- **Remote:** Employees outside that radius, including employees based in New York and Washington, where we have no office.

Office locations are Austin, San Jose, and Chicago. Managers may not independently change these classifications or authorize unapproved work locations.

## Office attendance

Hybrid employees must work from their assigned office Tuesday through Thursday and may work remotely Monday and Friday. Onsite employees follow their assigned office schedule.

Office attendance is not required during approved leave, company holidays, approved business travel, or an approved exception. Missed days for these reasons do not automatically require makeup days.

Remote employees may be asked to attend planned business meetings. Managers must give reasonable notice; necessary business-travel expenses and compensable travel time are handled under company policy and applicable law.

## Working from another location (in the US and abroad)

Employees may request temporary work from another location for up to four scheduled workweeks per calendar year, normally 20 workdays, across US and overseas locations combined. This is not an automatic entitlement.

Obtain written manager and People approval **before** working away from your approved home worksite or assigned office. Provide the location, dates, and proposed working hours. Approval depends on payroll, tax, employment-law, security, and business requirements. Temporary approval may excuse normal office attendance for the approved dates.

- **Within the US:** People must confirm that the company can support employment in the proposed state.
- **Abroad:** Work is permitted only in **Canada or the UK**, and only after People and counsel approve the specific arrangement. Employees must have lawful permission to work there. An existing company entity or employer-of-record does not guarantee approval.

Employees must remain available during agreed working hours and use approved equipment and secure connections. Vacation approval is not permission to work abroad. Company-required business travel does not count toward the four-week allowance but still requires applicable approvals.

## Changing your home state

Your approved home state remains your primary residence and work state. Request People approval at least **60 days before** a permanent interstate move. Do not begin working from the new state until written approval is issued.

Approval depends on the company’s ability to meet legal and operational requirements. A move may change your work arrangement. Temporary-location approval does not authorize permanent relocation.

## Equipment and expense reimbursement (with state-specific rules)

The company supplies required computing equipment. Employees must protect company equipment and information and return equipment when requested.

All employees receive a **$50 monthly home-office stipend**, without receipts for that payment. It is not a reimbursement ceiling.

If actual, necessary work expenses exceed the amount covered by the stipend and any direct company payment, submit a shortfall claim. Claims must identify the expense, amount, and business purpose and include receipts or other reasonable evidence. If documentation is unavailable, provide a signed explanation. People will help determine a reasonable work-related share of mixed personal and business expenses, including phone and internet.

Request approval before unusual purchases when practicable. Lack of advance approval will not defeat reimbursement required by law. The former 50%-of-bill formula and $60 cap no longer apply.

| State | Default arrangement | Expense rules |
|---|---|---|
| California | Within 50 miles: hybrid; otherwise remote, unless designated onsite | $50 stipend plus all necessary expense shortfalls under California law; no cap on legally required reimbursement. |
| Illinois | Within 50 miles: hybrid; otherwise remote, unless designated onsite | $50 stipend plus necessary employment-related shortfalls. Submit documented claims within 60 days of incurring the expense; People may allow longer periods. |
| Texas | Within 50 miles: hybrid; otherwise remote, unless designated onsite | $50 stipend plus necessary expense shortfalls under this policy and applicable law. |
| New York | Remote | $50 stipend plus necessary expense shortfalls under this policy and applicable law. |
| Washington | Remote | $50 stipend plus necessary expense shortfalls under this policy and applicable law. |

Approved exceptions may alter these arrangements. Expenses must not unlawfully reduce minimum-wage or overtime pay. Questions or disputed claims should go to People.

## Hours, timekeeping and non-exempt employees

Employees must follow their agreed schedule and applicable meal and rest-break requirements.

Non-exempt employees must record **all time worked**, including required computer startup, VPN access, system login, shutdown, after-hours messages, and other job tasks. Begin recording time before required startup activities; use the approved alternative recording method if the timekeeping system is not yet accessible.

Do not work off the clock. Obtain advance approval for overtime or schedule changes, but record all work even if it was not authorized. The company will pay all compensable time; unauthorized work may be addressed separately. Report missed or interrupted meal periods and timekeeping errors promptly.

## Exceptions and accommodations

Request exceptions through your manager and People. People must approve exceptions in writing, including their duration and review date.

Employees needing disability, pregnancy-related, religious, or other legally protected accommodations should contact People. The company will evaluate requests through the applicable accommodation process. No employee will face retaliation for requesting an accommodation, reporting unpaid work, or seeking required reimbursement.

## Policy owner and effective date

**Owner:** People, working with Finance, IT, and counsel.

**Effective date:** The launch date approved by the CEO and communicated by People. Applicable law controls if it provides greater employee protections.

---

### Note to the CEO

I retained Tuesday–Thursday attendance and used the existing 50-mile threshold to define “near.”

I departed from three instructions. The $50 stipend cannot replace necessary-expense reimbursement: California requires shortfall reimbursement, and Illinois requires reimbursement under a compliant written policy. Routine stipend payments need no receipts, but supplemental claims need reasonable documentation. I extended shortfall coverage company-wide for consistency.

Required startup and VPN login time must be paid for non-exempt employees under counsel’s wage-hour guidance.

“Work from anywhere” is approval-based, not unconditional. Overseas work is limited to Canada and the UK, with counsel review, because even short stays can create immigration, tax, and corporate exposure.

Please approve the 50-mile definition, company-wide shortfall reimbursement and its budget, the overseas restrictions, and a handbook launch date. The existing 60-day relocation approval requirement remains.
